key_insight: MACE-driven molecular dynamics reproduces overall DFT sorption trends for point defects in 2D materials, with qualitative trends largely unchanged at 300 K.
engineering_relevance: Low-cost ML-potential simulations enable high-throughput prescreening of defect sorption behavior before expensive first-principles validation.
method: Select 17,624 defect structures from the ADAQ database.
Use MACE to simulate structures at 0 K and 300 K.
Compare adsorption-versus-absorption trends with prior DFT results.
evidence_signal: Across 17,624 structures, MACE reproduced overall DFT sorption trends at 0 K, while 300 K simulations showed largely consistent qualitative behavior.
watch_item: Agreement in aggregate sorption trends does not establish quantitative accuracy for individual defects; DFT validation remains necessary.
paper_title: Sorption Molecular Dynamics of Point Defects in 2D Materials with a Machine Learning Potential
